info.title: Pharos receiver protocol
info.description: Implemented by a service that receives data from Pharos exporters, such as Pythia's. Pharos always initiates: after registration the receiver only answers. Each run is hello, then batches, then commit; only a committed run is acknowledged. The receiver may ask Pharos to send changes, everything, or particular items again, but never for more than the plugin's consented permissions.

post.summary: Start a run and say what the receiver needs
post.description: A receipt the receiver does not recognize means it lost what came after, and it answers everything. Outside a takeover, a known receipt older than the latest is explained only by unconfirmed_run naming the run that produced the latest; anything else means two libraries are sending as one instance, refused with 409 forked.

409.description: conflict: permissions_hash differs from the consented one (the person updates the plugin); superseded: library_instance was replaced by a takeover, or is unknown and names no takeover (this copy of the library stops sending); forked: the receipt shows another library sending as this instance (this copy stops sending until it is recovered as its own library)

post.summary: Stage one batch of the run

parameters.name: Pharos-Batch-SHA256
parameters.description: sha256: of the body. The same Idempotency-Key with a different hash is refused with 409 batch_conflict.

422.description: A field outside the installation's consented permissions; names the field

409.description: batch_conflict: this key was staged with different content

post.description: Staged until commit. A retried run always has a new run_id, so one key always means one body. Batches never committed are discarded after 24 hours.

post.summary: Apply the run's batches together and return a receipt
post.description: Upserts and periods apply when newer than what is stored and than any tombstone; retractions delete content and keep a tombstone; a period replaces every group of its (series, period). Nothing is removed by absence, except at the commit that completes a takeover, which retracts whatever no run of that takeover sent.

409.description: A batch is missing; Pharos runs again with a new run_id

delete.description: Sent after the optional last run that retracts everything. What the receiver keeps afterwards is its own policy.

post.summary: registration.token_url: exchange the authorization code, or refresh
post.description: OAuth 2.0 for native apps (RFC 8252). Pharos opens registration.url with response_type=code, client_id (the plugin ID), a loopback redirect_uri, state, code_challenge with S256, and sender_id, permissions_hash and any invitation code from the install link. The path here is illustrative; the manifest names the real one.

accessToken.description: An access token from registration, scoped to one installation: it can say hello, deliver and commit, and nothing else.

Disconnected.description: The person disconnected on the receiver's side, or access was revoked; Pharos pauses the plugin with a notice
